title: Elevate Your Career: Join the Next Gen Hub
content:
# ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/f760ee3144a24710aaa6176173f82111/images/59c466a6b39244ea879e839df2617edaNGH%20small%202.jpg)**Next Gen Hub**

**Showcase Your Talent, Unlock Opportunities**

The **Next Gen Hub** is a curated space designed to highlight the next generation of creative leaders. We provide students and early-career creators with a professional platform to spotlight their work, gain industry recognition, and connect directly with companies seeking fresh talent.

![13b7a07daf6d4678a350a09905bf3b7f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/f760ee3144a24710aaa6176173f82111/images/13b7a07daf6d4678a350a09905bf3b7fimage%20%287%29.png)

## **Are you ready to join?**

We are looking for passionate creators who are ready to make their mark. You are eligible if you fall into any of the following categories:

  * **Students or Recent Graduates**




Currently enrolled in or newly graduated from a design or creative field.  


  * **Self-Taught Visionaries**




Independent creators building their first professional portfolio.  


  * **Career Explorers:**




Professionals transitioning into a brand-new creative discipline.

  
Your CONNECT portfolio must demonstrate high levels of creativity, technical skill, and growth potential. 

We also require all members to be active participants within the CONNECT community.

## **What You'll Get**

  * **Featured placement** in CONNECT Creator for maximum visibility.  


  * **Direct exposure** to Enterprise clients seeking new talent.  


  * **Promotion** across CLO, Marvelous Designer social channels and community.  


  * **Exclusive invitations** to mentorships, events, and spotlight campaigns.  





## **How to Apply**

To be considered for a featured placement:

\- Make sure you have an active CONNECT profile.

\- Prepare your portfolio.

\- Submit your application through the link below:

  


# **[**[**Submit your Application**](https://form.asana.com/?k=P5tPSm5ykxX5wQ5E9mhlag&d=78618343223729)**]**

## **Review Process:**

  * Applications are reviewed by Design members to ensure candidates meet the defined criteria. 

  * Evaluation metrics are tracked internally for consistency and transparency.

  * **If your profile is selected, you will receive an email notification and you will see your work featured directly in the Hub tab.**




## **Community Guidelines:**

To stay in the Hub, members must:

  * Respectful communication and professional conduct.

  * Sharing only original content or work you have rights to publish.

  * No offensive, discriminatory, or plagiarized material.

  * No use or promotion of illegal or pirated tools/software.

  * Collaboration and feedback should remain constructive and respectful.




## **License Compliance:**

  * All participants must use valid and legal software licenses.



  * Use of cracked or pirated versions is strictly prohibited.




🚫 Use of unlicensed or cracked software, or violation of community rules, may result in removal from the Next Gen Hub and CONNECT.

  


* * *

  


**LEGAL DISCLAIMER & TERMS OF PARTICIPATION**

By submitting an application to the Next Gen Hub, you ("the Participant") acknowledge that you have read, understood, and agree to be bound by the following terms and conditions:

**1\. Nature of the Initiative.** The Next Gen Hub is a promotional initiative and community-building program operated by CLO Virtual Fashion. It is designed solely to increase the visibility of emerging talent and to foster the growth of the CLO user community. The Next Gen Hub is not a separate legal entity, subsidiary, partnership, or joint venture. It functions strictly as a curated showcase and referral resource. CLO Virtual Fashion does not act as a staffing agency, headhunter, or commercial intermediary between Participants and Enterprise clients.

**2\. No Employment or Agency Relationship.** Participation in the Next Gen Hub is voluntary and does not constitute an employment contract, independent contractor agreement, or agency relationship between the Participant and CLO Virtual Fashion.

**2.1 No Compensation.** Selection for the Hub does not entitle the Participant to any wages, benefits, insurance, or compensation from CLO Virtual Fashion.

**2.2 No Guarantee of Work.** While the Hub aims to facilitate connections, CLO Virtual Fashion makes no representations or warranties regarding the availability of internships, freelance work, or full-time employment resulting from this visibility.

**3\. Adherence to General Terms of Use.** These Terms of Participation constitute "Additional Terms" as defined in CLO Virtual Fashion’s General Terms of Use. By participating in this initiative, you acknowledge that your access to and use of the Services (including CLO-SET and CLO-SET Connect) remain governed by the General Terms of Use (<https://legal.clo-set.com/general>). As established in the General Terms of Use, in the event of any conflict between these Terms and the General Terms of Use regarding the Next Gen Hub, these Terms shall prevail, while all non-conflicting provisions of the General Terms of Use shall remain in full force and effect.

**4\. Software Compliance & Ethical Conduct:**

**4.1 Licensing.** The Participant warrants that all work submitted and displayed has been created using valid, legally licensed software. The use of cracked, pirated, or unauthorized versions of CLO software (or any third-party tools) is strictly prohibited and constitutes a material breach of these terms, resulting in immediate removal and potential legal action.

**4.2 Community Guidelines.** The Participant agrees to adhere to the CONNECT Community Guidelines. Any conduct deemed offensive, discriminatory, unprofessional, or harassing will result in immediate termination from the initiative.

**5\. Intellectual Property & Usage Rights:**

**5.1 Ownership.** The Participant retains full ownership and copyright of their original work.

**5.2 License to Display.** By participating, the Participant grants CLO Virtual Fashion a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, and perpetual license to reproduce, display, distribute, and promote the submitted portfolio materials on CLO’s platforms (including CONNECT), social media channels, and marketing materials for the specific purpose of promoting the Participant and the Next Gen Hub initiative.

**5.3 Originality.** The Participant warrants that their work is original and does not infringe upon the intellectual property rights, privacy rights, or other legal rights of any third party.

**6\. Active Status & Removal:**

**6.1 Engagement.** Continued participation is conditional upon active community engagement (minimum of two meaningful interactions per month).

**6.2 Right to Remove.** CLO Virtual Fashion reserves the absolute right to remove any Participant from the Next Gen Hub at any time, for any reason, without prior notice or liability.

**6.3 Periodic Review.** Profiles are subject to review every 3 months. Accounts inactive for more than 6 months may be offboarded to maintain the quality of the Hub.

**7\. Data Privacy & Processing.** Personal data and portfolio information collected for the Next Gen Hub will be processed in accordance with CLO Virtual Fashion’s Privacy Policy. The Participant explicitly consents to their profile data being shared with third-party Enterprise clients for the purpose of professional introductions.

**8\. Voluntary Withdrawal.** The Participant may request the removal of their profile from the Next Gen Hub at any time by submitting a formal request via the "Contact Us" form on the CLO or MD website. CLO Virtual Fashion will process such requests and cease the feature of the profile within a commercially reasonable timeframe.
content_description: The Next Gen Hub web page provides a professional platform for emerging creative talents to showcase their portfolios, gain industry exposure, and connect with potential employers and mentors within the CLO Virtual Fashion community.

title: Python API ImportAvatarMeasurement() always returns False on Mac + headless video export
content:
Hi everyone,

I'm a PhD student at UC Davis using CLO 2025.2.330 Standalone Academic on Mac. I'm building an ML dataset of garment simulation videos across different body shapes using the Python API. I've contacted CLO support (ticket 135471) and they directed me here. I have two blockers I can't resolve:

Issue 1: ImportAvatarMeasurement() always returns False

I have tried every combination of .avs and .avt files including:

  * US_ASTM Missy/Petite/Plus .avs files with FV2.1_Yuna.avt

  * Custom-saved .avs files with FV2.1_Yuna.avt

  * Exported mannequin .avt with various .avs files




Code used:

import import_api, ApiTypes

opt = ApiTypes.ImportExportOption()

result = import_api.ImportAvatarMeasurement(avs_path, avt_path, opt)

print(result) # always False

Issue 2: ExportAnimationVideo() cannot save headlessly on Mac

ExportAnimationVideo(path) always opens a Qt dialog that cannot be automated. Calling with no arguments returns a path but the file is never written (no Xvid codec on Mac). How do we export animation videos headlessly from Python on Mac?

Any working code examples would be greatly appreciated.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, ajrichardsonThe ImportAvatarMeasurement API is currently implemented to be available for enterprise customers.Upon checking, ExportAnimationVideo is implemented to simply open the dialog for that feature. We will internally discuss providing a new API for this functionality.
content_description: A resource page for troubleshooting CLO 3D Python API issues related to avatar measurement import failures and headless animation video export on Mac.

title: Render stopped!!
content:
Hello!

I let my macbook pro rendering all night but it stopped. I’m doing a turntable animation. And it’s weird cause the rendering clock is still going but the progress is frozen.

Do i have to restart the rendering? 😭😭![74581d6e7fef43858a07ff7d2465731d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/1a77632b39ec4061bbb3708337e61cc6/images/74581d6e7fef43858a07ff7d2465731dIMG_2371.jpeg)![3a9cf701935d41d8b97aa203bce56838](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/1a77632b39ec4061bbb3708337e61cc6/images/3a9cf701935d41d8b97aa203bce56838IMG_2372.jpeg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you all for the response!! I had no idea i could re render the remaining frames i'll definitely try that

Comment 2: Yes, that's right. You can check if there are sequence frame pictures in the folder you specified. If so, you only need to re - render the remaining dozen or so pictures. It seems that it's relatively stable on Mac. You can render so many frames at once, while on Windows, it gets stuck when rendering over a hundred frames.

Comment 3: From the picture, it seems that the render for 346 sheets is completed. If you check CLO Asset Folder, the image will exist. I think you only need to proceed with the additional 14 sheets of render after it stopped working.You must have been worried a lot because a lot of time has passed, but I hope you don't worry too much.Cheer up!👏
content_description: A support page to help users troubleshoot and resolve MacBook Pro rendering issues during turntable animation projects.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi robin.wag,Sorry to hear about your difficulty signing in to CLO.This issue is typically caused by cached browser data conflicting with your integrated CLO-SET account. To resolve this, please log out of the software and all CLO websites, clear your browser cache, and restart the program. When prompted, select the "Sign in with CLO-SET" option rather than entering your credentials manually.If the issue continues, please submit a ticket at www.clo3d.com/en/support/contactus for further investigation.

title: DXF AAMA export loses annotations
content:
I'm trying to export in DXF format for use in Gerber and if I export a graded pattern, it grades on the sewing lines instead of the seam allowance. I can export individually (what a pain) but the annotations do not stay connected to the patterns. They are off in space. Now I'm stuck with a lot of patterns made for a client which I can't make in a format they can use, help.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Is your client using the Gerber Data Exchange Utility and selecting the "Grade on Sew Line" option during import? Since CLO anchors grading to the sewing line, this setting is required for Gerber to correctly read the nest and maintain the seam allowances, which are preserved as distinct coordinate data within the DXF-AAMA file.If this doesn't resolve the issue, please upload the file to our technical support portal for a deeper look: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/e53750502b674a94a09412ea375f6619

Comment 2: So, this is all in the CLO zpri file. It also doesn't show the seam allowance graded here, but when I switch sizes it shows the correct seam allowance so I know the data is there.

Comment 3: Hi carfritsch,Happy to help! Could you attach screenshots of your export settings, and the 2d window showing the patterns with seam allowance with grading on and off?
content_description: This page provides solutions for correctly exporting graded patterns in DXF format with accurate seam allowance grading and properly connected annotations for use in Gerber systems.

title: Game Inspired Character Outfit — Recreated in Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/69f213cd187f4c0284ba3e11354e4c07INVISIB_19.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/23f5f0319f4b4022bb76e1f0681a751bINVISIB_19.png)Invisible Women Inspired Outfit — Marvelous Designer Project

While playing a game, I came across a character skin that immediately caught my attention because of its **bold colors, retro style, and strong character personality**. The design felt unique and stylish, and I wanted to challenge myself by recreating a similar outfit using **Marvelous Designer**.

This project became an opportunity to explore how a **game-inspired costume** could be translated into a garment created entirely through digital pattern making and cloth simulation.

![7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15Screenshot%20%28505%29.png)

* * *

### Reference and Inspiration

The main inspiration for this outfit came from Marvel Rivals **game character skin**. What stood out to me the most was the combination of:

  * Bright pink color palette

  * Retro fashion elements

  * Futuristic character styling




The design balances **playful fashion with a confident hero-like presence** , which made it an interesting challenge to recreate.

### Building the Outfit in Marvelous Designer

The outfit was constructed step by step inside Marvelous Designer using pattern-based garment creation.

The process started with the **base pants and top** , carefully fitted to the avatar to establish a clean silhouette. Once the foundation was working correctly, additional pieces were layered to build the final look.

Key garment pieces include:

  * A **structured corset-style top** with panel segmentation

  * **High-waisted pants** with curved seam lines

  * A **short cropped jacket** to add structure and contrast

  * A **scarf accessory** to introduce movement to the design




Each piece was simulated and adjusted to maintain a natural garment flow.

![64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00bScreenshot%20%28534%29.png)

### Details and Character Elements

To capture the personality of the original inspiration, several stylistic elements were incorporated:

  * A decorative **belt with circular details and emblem**

  * Retro-inspired **sunglasses**

  * Flowing lower pant sections that soften the silhouette




These elements help create a design that feels **stylish, playful, and character-driven**.

![f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238INVISIB_19.png)

![606c628ae36340e886989db582082cca](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/606c628ae36340e886989db582082ccaINVISIB_21.png)

### Final Thoughts

This project was mainly a **practice and exploration piece** , inspired by a game skin that I enjoyed while playing. Recreating it in Marvelous Designer helped me better understand **pattern construction, garment layering, and digital clothing simulation**.

It was a fun challenge to translate a **stylized game costume into a simulated garment** , and it allowed me to experiment with both **fashion design and character outfit creation**.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: This is awesome! I want to jump into The Sims right now and put this on my Sim.
Reply 1: That’s such a compliment, thanks😍
content_description: Showcasing the digital recreation of a vibrant, retro-inspired game character outfit using Marvelous Designer to explore pattern making and cloth simulation.
